name: Breaking Bricks News — daily episode (front-end for the YakYak engine)

parameters.content:
## 📄 YakYak Description — workflow summary (not a step note)
Every day at UTC 06:00 the Middle Eastern news from CNN, BBC and Al Jazeera are fetched. The articles are weaved into a plot and rendered by LEGO characters.

nodes.name: Every morning
nodes.notes: 06:00 UTC daily — CADENCE=daily in show/BreakingBricksNews/show.env. Use 'Test workflow' to fire a run by hand.

nodes.name: Show config
nodes.notes: ALL per-show config lives here, on the canvas — the workflow reads no environment variables. Required: campaignId (a campaign the API credential's account owns) and userId (for the balance check). Optional: soundtrackAudioPath (prefilled with the BBN intro track's content address — the beta/ prefix is normal, see docs/forking.md; empty = skip the pin), chatWebhookUrl (empty = no announcement). postToSocial=true is POST="true" parity — every run publishes to the campaign's linked networks (irreversible); set false for review-first runs.

nodes.name: Fetch user
nodes.notes: Same 'YakYak API' Bearer credential as the engine — no token on the canvas or in env. onError=continue so Balance guard can report a clear error instead of a bare 404.

nodes.name: Fetch BBC
nodes.notes: Server-rendered RSS — titles + pubDate. onError=continue: a blocked source must not kill the run (the prompt says to proceed with what it has).

nodes.name: Fetch CNN
nodes.notes: CNN's no-JS site. The prompt keeps only /middleeast/ links; dates are baked into the URLs.

parameters.jsCode:
// The BBN head-writer prompt, adapted from show/BreakingBricksNews/prompt.md.
// Two changes vs the showrunner original: STEP 1's agentic WebFetch is replaced
// by the source material the three fetch nodes just pulled (an API call can't
// fetch the web itself), and STEP 4's file-write becomes "reply with only the
// markdown". A '## Social title:' line is requested so ONE model call covers
// both the story and the ≤50-char social title the showrunner made separately.
const trim = (s) => String(s || '').slice(0, 15000);
const src = (label, s) => s ? `--- ${label} ---\n${s}` : `--- ${label} ---\n(source unavailable this run — proceed without it)`;
const bbc = trim(($('Fetch BBC').first().json || {}).data);
const cnn = trim(($('Fetch CNN').first().json || {}).data);
const aj = trim(($('Fetch AJ').first().json || {}).data);
if (!bbc && !cnn && !aj) throw new Error('all three news sources failed to fetch — aborting (no material for an episode)');
const ts = new Date().toISOString();

const prompt = `You are the head writer for "Breaking Bricks News", a dark-comedy short-form
video series that is grounded in real Middle East events but voiced with
tongue-in-cheek bite. Your job in this run is to produce ONE story.

STEP 1 — Read the news. The fetched source material is included below
(BBC Middle East RSS, CNN Lite front page, Al Jazeera Middle East page).
  - BBC: read the RSS <pubDate> on each <item> for the timestamp.
  - CNN: use only links under the "/middleeast/" path. The date is baked into
    each URL (e.g. /2026/07/02/middleeast/...) — use that date as the timestamp.
    Ignore non-Middle-East stories.
  - Al Jazeera: use the Middle East feed items.
Only keep items whose timestamp falls within the past 24 hours (now: ${ts}).
If a source is marked unavailable, note it and proceed with what you have.

STEP 2 — Pick the threads. From the 24h headlines, choose 3–6 real developments
that can be woven into a single narrative arc. Prefer items that touch more
than one of our cast.

STEP 3 — Write the story.

CAST (only these may speak; the "leading character" of each scene must be one of them):
  - Bob Brikko — our fearless Breaking Bricks News field reporter.
    MUST be the leading character in Scene 1 (cold open) and Scene 10 (sign-off).
    Tongue-in-cheek, dry, deadpan under fire.
  - Donald Trump
  - Benjamin Netanyahu
  - Mojtaba Khamenei (the Iranian Supreme Leader's son, not Ali)
  - An Israeli fighter pilot (unnamed, call her/him "The Pilot")

TONE: Dark comedy. Real headline beats drive the plot; the humor comes from the
characters' voice, framing, and reaction shots. No slapstick, no cartoon
villainy, no slurs. Punch up, not down.

PER-SCENE REQUIREMENTS:
  - Roughly 200 words of prose describing the scene's visuals, action, and
    atmosphere (location, what we see, what just happened, what's happening
    now). Write it as a director would brief a camera op.
  - Exactly ONE spoken dialog line per scene, 8–12 words, attributed to the
    scene's leading character. Do NOT end the dialog line with a period
    ("!" or "?" are fine).
  - Leading character must be from the cast. No other characters speak.

STEP 4 — Reply with ONLY the markdown document below — no preamble, no
triple-backtick fences, nothing after it:

  # Breaking Bricks News — Latest Update
  **Generated (UTC):** ${ts}
  **Sources:** BBC / CNN / Al Jazeera (Middle East), past 24h

  ## Social title: <punchy title for social posting, 50 characters MAX>

  ## Headlines we drew from:
  - <one bullet per real event you used, each with the source it came from>

  ## Scene 1 — <short title>
  **Leading character:** Bob Brikko
  **Dialog:** "<8–12 word line>"

  <~200 words of scene prose>

  ... (continue through Scene 10, which is again Bob Brikko) ...

===== SOURCE MATERIAL =====

${src('BBC Middle East RSS', bbc)}

${src('CNN Lite', cnn)}

${src('Al Jazeera Middle East', aj)}`;

return [{ json: { prompt } }];

nodes.name: Write story (Claude)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'claude-opus-4-8', max_tokens: 16000, thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, messages: [ { role: 'user', content: $json.prompt } ] } }}

nodes.notes: Messages API over raw HTTP (no SDK inside n8n). Auth via the 'Anthropic API key' Header Auth credential (header name x-api-key). Adaptive thinking; the story lands in the response's text block.

nodes.name: Build story payload
nodes.notes: The story markdown is preserved on this node's output — n8n's execution log is the story archive (the showrunner's stories/ equivalent).

nodes.name: Call engine

workflowId.cachedResultName: YakYak engine — resolve target, patch or new episode, render, post

nodes.notes: Fires the generic YakYak engine in episode mode. Timeout 45 min — the engine only responds once the episode is generated AND rendered. Retry is safe: a re-run lands on the same unrendered slot. Announcement happens here (below), not in the engine.

nodes.name: Set social fields

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ Object.assign({ movieId: $json.movieId }, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle ? { socialTitle: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle } : {}, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption ? { socialDescription: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption } : {}) }}

nodes.notes: Showrunner parity: ≤50-char social title (from the story call) + headline-derived caption. onError=continue — cosmetic metadata must not kill a rendered episode.

nodes.name: Announce

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { text: '🧱 BBN episode ready — "' + ($('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle || 'Latest Update') + '": ' + $('Call engine').item.json.url } }}

nodes.notes: Chat notification with the episode link. chatWebhookUrl empty → this node errors and the run still succeeds (onError=continue). Social posting happens in the three nodes after this one, gated by Show config postToSocial — see integrations/n8n/docs/breaking_bricks_news.md §4.3.

nodes.name: Fetch campaign links
nodes.notes: The campaign's linked social networks — GET /social/campaign-links, same call the showrunner makes before posting. Read-only, so it runs regardless; the postToSocial gate is applied in Build post list. onError=continue so Build post list can report a clear error.

nodes.name: Build post list
nodes.notes: One item per linked network. Linking networks to the campaign is a one-time manual step (yakyak.ai profile, or course/08-social-post) — with none linked, this emits zero items and the run still succeeds.

nodes.name: Post to socials
nodes.notes: POST /social/post-movie/{movieId}/{connectedNetworkId}, empty body — runs once per item, i.e. once per linked network. IRREVERSIBLE. onError=continue mirrors the showrunner: a per-network 4xx (mis-configured account etc.) must not fail the other networks or the run. Needs the social_publishing scope on the PAT.
